function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

I will start by analyzing the sales data for Q3 2024, which covers the period from July 1, 2024, to September 30, 2024. The analysis will include:

1. Total revenue for the whole period.
2. Total revenue per month of the period (July, August, September).

arguments.code:
import json
import pandas as pd
from datetime import datetime

# Load the data
with open('./runtime_data/2024-07-01_to_2024-09-30_order.json') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

# Initialize lists to store revenue data
revenue_data = []

# Process each order
for order in orders:
    processed_at = order['node']['processedAt']
    total_price = float(order['node']['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    revenue_data.append({'date': processed_at, 'total_price': total_price})

# Create a DataFrame
revenue_df = pd.DataFrame(revenue_data)

# Convert 'date' to datetime
revenue_df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(revenue_df['date'])

# Set date as index
revenue_df.set_index('date', inplace=True)

# Calculate total revenue for the whole period
total_revenue = revenue_df['total_price'].sum()

include_domains.description:

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:

        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics,

        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:

        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by

I will start by analyzing the sales data for Q3 2024, which covers the period from July 1, 2024, to September 30, 2024. The analysis will include:

1. Total revenue for the whole period.
2. Total revenue per month of the period (July, August, September).

To do this, I will first load the data from the saved JSON file and then perform the necessary calculations.

Let's proceed with the analysis.

arguments.code:
import json
import pandas as pd
from datetime import datetime

# Load the data
with open('./runtime_data/2024-07-01_to_2024-09-30_order.json') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

# Initialize lists to store revenue data
revenue_data = []

# Process each order
for order in orders:
    processed_at = order['node']['processedAt']
    total_price = float(order['node']['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    revenue_data.append({'date': processed_at, 'total_price': total_price})

# Create a DataFrame
revenue_df = pd.DataFrame(revenue_data)

# Convert 'date' to datetime
revenue_df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(revenue_df['date'])

# Set date as index
revenue_df.set_index('date', inplace=True)

# Calculate total revenue for the whole period
total_revenue = revenue_df['total_price'].sum()

# Calculate total revenue per month
monthly_revenue = revenue_df.resample('M').sum()

# Calculate quarterly revenue
quarterly_revenue = revenue_df.resample('Q').sum()

# Calculate revenue trend
monthly_trend = monthly_revenue['total_price'].tolist()
quarterly_trend = quarterly_revenue['total_price'].tolist()

# Prepare the results
results = {
    'total_revenue': total_revenue,
    'monthly_revenue': monthly_revenue['total_price'].to_dict(),
    'quarterly_revenue': quarterly_revenue['total_price'].to_dict(),
    'monthly_trend': monthly_trend,
    'quarterly_trend': quarterly_trend
}

# Print the results
print(results)

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

# Process each order
for order in orders_data:
    total_orders += 1
    processed_date = order['node']['processedAt']

    'monthly_orders': dict(monthly_orders),
    'average_spent_overall': average_spent_overall,
    'average_spent_monthly': average_spent_monthly
}

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

    'monthly_orders': dict(monthly_orders),

    processed_date = order['node']['processedAt']

    total_price = float(order['node']['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])

    monthly_spent[month] += total_price

average_spent_monthly = {month: (monthly_spent[month] / monthly_orders[month]) if monthly_orders[month] > 0 else 0 for month in monthly_orders}

# Prepare results
results = {
    'total_orders': total_orders,
    'monthly_orders': dict(monthly_orders),
    'average_spent_overall': average_spent_overall,

import json

from collections import defaultdict

# Process each order
for order in orders_data:
    total_orders += 1
    processed_date = order['node']['processedAt']

    monthly_spent[month] += total_price

# Calculate average spent per order overall

# Calculate average spent per order trend for each month

# Prepare results
results = {
    'total_orders': total_orders,
    'monthly_orders': dict(monthly_orders),
    'average_spent_overall': average_spent_overall,
    'average_spent_monthly': average_spent_monthly
}

print(results)

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

1. Identifying the top and bottom overall products based on sales.
2. Identifying the top and bottom products sold per month.

import json
import pandas as pd
from datetime import datetime

# Load the data
with open('./runtime_data/2024-07-01_to_2024-09-30_order.json') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

# Prepare a list to hold all line items for analysis
line_items = []

# Extract relevant information from each order
for order in orders:
    processed_at = order['node']['processedAt']
    total_price = float(order['node']['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    for item in order['node']['lineItems']['edges']:
        title = item['node']['title']
        quantity = item['node']['quantity']
        line_items.append({
            'title': title,
            'quantity': quantity,
            'total_price': total_price,
            'processed_at': processed_at
        })

# Create a DataFrame for analysis
df = pd.DataFrame(line_items)

# Convert processed_at to datetime and extract month

df['processed_at'] = pd.to_datetime(df['processed_at'])
df['month'] = df['processed_at'].dt.to_period('M')

# Calculate total sales per product
product_sales = df.groupby('title').agg(total_quantity=('quantity', 'sum'), total_revenue=('total_price', 'sum')).reset_index()

# Identify top and bottom overall products
overall_top_product = product_sales.loc[product_sales['total_revenue'].idxmax()]
overall_bottom_product = product_sales.loc[product_sales['total_revenue'].idxmin()]

# Calculate monthly sales
monthly_sales = df.groupby(['month', 'title']).agg(total_quantity=('quantity', 'sum'), total_revenue=('total_price', 'sum')).reset_index()

# Identify top and bottom products per month
monthly_top_bottom_products = monthly_sales.groupby('month').agg(
    top_product=('total_revenue', 'idxmax'),
    bottom_product=('total_revenue', 'idxmin')
).reset_index()

# Merge to get product names
monthly_top_bottom_products = monthly_top_bottom_products.merge(monthly_sales, left_on=['month', 'top_product'], right_index=True)
monthly_top_bottom_products = monthly_top_bottom_products.merge(monthly_sales, left_on=['month', 'bottom_product'], right_index=True,
    suffixes=('_top', '_bottom'))

# Identify top and bottom revenue contributor products
revenue_contributors = product_sales.sort_values(by='total_revenue', ascending=False)

# Prepare final results
results = {
    'overall_top_product': overall_top_product.to_dict(),
    'overall_bottom_product': overall_bottom_product.to_dict(),
    'monthly_top_bottom_products': monthly_top_bottom_products[['month', 'title_top', 'total_revenue_top', 'title_bottom', 'total_revenue_bottom']].to_dict(orient='records'),
    'top_revenue_contributor': revenue_contributors.iloc[0].to_dict(),
    'bottom_revenue_contributor': revenue_contributors.iloc[-1].to_dict()
}

# Print results
print(results)

import json
import pandas as pd
from datetime import datetime

# Load the data
with open('./runtime_data/2024-07-01_to_2024-09-30_order.json') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

# Prepare a list to hold all line items for analysis
line_items = []

# Extract relevant information from each order
for order in orders:
    processed_at = order['node']['processedAt']
    total_price = float(order['node']['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    for item in order['node']['lineItems']['edges']:
        title = item['node']['title']
        quantity = item['node']['quantity']
        line_items.append({
            'title': title,
            'quantity': quantity,
            'total_price': total_price,
            'processed_at': processed_at
        })

# Create a DataFrame for analysis
df = pd.DataFrame(line_items)

# Convert processed_at to datetime and extract month

df['processed_at'] = pd.to_datetime(df['processed_at'])
df['month'] = df['processed_at'].dt.to_period('M')

# Calculate total sales per product
product_sales = df.groupby('title').agg(total_quantity=('quantity', 'sum'), total_revenue=('total_price', 'sum')).reset_index()

# Identify top and bottom overall products
overall_top_product = product_sales.loc[product_sales['total_revenue'].idxmax()]
overall_bottom_product = product_sales.loc[product_sales['total_revenue'].idxmin()]

# Calculate monthly sales
monthly_sales = df.groupby(['month', 'title']).agg(total_quantity=('quantity', 'sum'), total_revenue=('total_price', 'sum')).reset_index()

# Identify top and bottom products per month
monthly_top_bottom_products = monthly_sales.groupby('month').agg(
    top_product=('total_revenue', 'idxmax'),
    bottom_product=('total_revenue', 'idxmin')
).reset_index()

# Merge to get product names
monthly_top_bottom_products = monthly_top_bottom_products.merge(monthly_sales, left_on=['month', 'top_product'], right_index=True)
monthly_top_bottom_products = monthly_top_bottom_products.merge(monthly_sales, left_on=['month', 'bottom_product'], right_index=True,
    suffixes=('_top', '_bottom'))

# Identify top and bottom revenue contributor products
revenue_contributors = product_sales.sort_values(by='total_revenue', ascending=False)

# Prepare final results
results = {
    'overall_top_product': overall_top_product.to_dict(),
    'overall_bottom_product': overall_bottom_product.to_dict(),
    'monthly_top_bottom_products': monthly_top_bottom_products[['month', 'title_top', 'total_revenue_top', 'title_bottom', 'total_revenue_bottom']].to_dict(orient='records'),
    'top_revenue_contributor': revenue_contributors.iloc[0].to_dict(),
    'bottom_revenue_contributor': revenue_contributors.iloc[-1].to_dict()
}

# Print results
print(results)

import json
import pandas as pd
from datetime import datetime

# Load the data
with open('./runtime_data/2024-07-01_to_2024-09-30_order.json') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

# Prepare a list to hold all line items for analysis
line_items = []

# Extract relevant information from each order
for order in orders:
    processed_at = order['node']['processedAt']
    total_price = float(order['node']['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    for item in order['node']['lineItems']['edges']:
        title = item['node']['title']
        quantity = item['node']['quantity']
        line_items.append({
            'title': title,
            'quantity': quantity,
            'total_price': total_price,
            'processed_at': processed_at
        })

# Create a DataFrame for analysis
df = pd.DataFrame(line_items)

# Convert processed_at to datetime and extract month

df['processed_at'] = pd.to_datetime(df['processed_at'])
df['month'] = df['processed_at'].dt.to_period('M')

# Calculate total sales per product
product_sales = df.groupby('title').agg(total_quantity=('quantity', 'sum'), total_revenue=('total_price', 'sum')).reset_index()

# Identify top and bottom overall products
overall_top_product = product_sales.loc[product_sales['total_revenue'].idxmax()]
overall_bottom_product = product_sales.loc[product_sales['total_revenue'].idxmin()]

# Calculate monthly sales
monthly_sales = df.groupby(['month', 'title']).agg(total_quantity=('quantity', 'sum'), total_revenue=('total_price', 'sum')).reset_index()

# Identify top and bottom products per month
monthly_top_bottom_products = monthly_sales.groupby('month').agg(
    top_product=('total_revenue', 'idxmax'),
    bottom_product=('total_revenue', 'idxmin')
).reset_index()

# Merge to get product names
monthly_top_bottom_products = monthly_top_bottom_products.merge(monthly_sales, left_on=['month', 'top_product'], right_index=True)
monthly_top_bottom_products = monthly_top_bottom_products.merge(monthly_sales, left_on=['month', 'bottom_product'], right_index=True,
    suffixes=('_top', '_bottom'))

# Identify top and bottom revenue contributor products
revenue_contributors = product_sales.sort_values(by='total_revenue', ascending=False)

# Prepare final results
results = {
    'overall_top_product': overall_top_product.to_dict(),
    'overall_bottom_product': overall_bottom_product.to_dict(),
    'monthly_top_bottom_products': monthly_top_bottom_products[['month', 'title_top', 'total_revenue_top', 'title_bottom', 'total_revenue_bottom']].to_dict(orient='records'),
    'top_revenue_contributor': revenue_contributors.iloc[0].to_dict(),
    'bottom_revenue_contributor': revenue_contributors.iloc[-1].to_dict()
}

# Print results
print(results)

import json
import pandas as pd
from datetime import datetime

# Load the data
with open('./runtime_data/2024-07-01_to_2024-09-30_order.json') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

# Prepare a list to hold all line items for analysis
line_items = []

# Extract relevant information from each order
for order in orders:
    processed_at = order['node']['processedAt']
    total_price = float(order['node']['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    for item in order['node']['lineItems']['edges']:
        title = item['node']['title']
        quantity = item['node']['quantity']
        line_items.append({
            'title': title,
            'quantity': quantity,
            'total_price': total_price,
            'processed_at': processed_at
        })

# Create a DataFrame for analysis
df = pd.DataFrame(line_items)

# Convert processed_at to datetime and extract month

df['processed_at'] = pd.to_datetime(df['processed_at'])
df['month'] = df['processed_at'].dt.to_period('M')

# Calculate total sales per product
product_sales = df.groupby('title').agg(total_quantity=('quantity', 'sum'), total_revenue=('total_price', 'sum')).reset_index()

# Identify top and bottom overall products
overall_top_product = product_sales.loc[product_sales['total_revenue'].idxmax()]
overall_bottom_product = product_sales.loc[product_sales['total_revenue'].idxmin()]

# Calculate monthly sales
monthly_sales = df.groupby(['month', 'title']).agg(total_quantity=('quantity', 'sum'), total_revenue=('total_price', 'sum')).reset_index()

# Identify top and bottom products per month
monthly_top_bottom_products = monthly_sales.groupby('month').agg(
    top_product=('total_revenue', 'idxmax'),
    bottom_product=('total_revenue', 'idxmin')
).reset_index()

# Merge to get product names
monthly_top_bottom_products = monthly_top_bottom_products.merge(monthly_sales, left_on=['month', 'top_product'], right_index=True)
monthly_top_bottom_products = monthly_top_bottom_products.merge(monthly_sales, left_on=['month', 'bottom_product'], right_index=True,
    suffixes=('_top', '_bottom'))

# Identify top and bottom revenue contributor products
revenue_contributors = product_sales.sort_values(by='total_revenue', ascending=False)

# Prepare final results
results = {
    'overall_top_product': overall_top_product.to_dict(),
    'overall_bottom_product': overall_bottom_product.to_dict(),
    'monthly_top_bottom_products': monthly_top_bottom_products[['month', 'title_top', 'total_revenue_top', 'title_bottom', 'total_revenue_bottom']].to_dict(orient='records'),
    'top_revenue_contributor': revenue_contributors.iloc[0].to_dict(),
    'bottom_revenue_contributor': revenue_contributors.iloc[-1].to_dict()
}

# Print results
print(results)

}

    'bottom_revenue_contributor': revenue_contributors.iloc[-1].to_dict()
}

}

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period

        You are a supervisor agent for final executive report writing, you will plan, manage agents, delegate specific agents to their tasks, and compile their output into draft of relevant informations, and write the final report. 
        What you need to write is sales report for a specific period of time of a shopify store Urban Thread, selling apparels and accessories.

        For a final annual executive report, it must have all of the item here:
        1. revenue report: total revenue, monthly revenue, trend, quarterly revenue (handoff to revenue analyst agent)
        2. order report: total number of order, number of order trend on each month, average spent per order, average spent per order trend on each month (handoff to order analyst agent)
        3. product performance: top/bottom overall product, top/bottom product per month, top/bottom revenue contributor product, top/bottom revenue contributor product per month (handoff to product performance analyst agent)
        4. strategic analyses: current report compared to annual strategy plan, target metrics vs actual realization metrics, met and unmet sales goal.
        
        To finish the final report, do this one by one

        1. First you must make plan on what to do. Summarize the request from the chat history. Write the period of final executive report requested.
        
        2. Retrieve the data you need using the tool get_order_data_for_period for the valid requested period, output the file name so that future agent know what the file name is.
        
        3. Only after retrieve the data in previous step, you will then delegate the revenue analysis to the revenue analyst agent by following this step:

### Strategic Analysis Report for Q3 2024

#### 1. Summarization of Goals and Targets from Annual Strategy Plan Documents for 2024:
The strategic goals outlined for 2024 include:
- **Increase annual revenue by 25%** to at least **£78,000**.
- **Grow total orders by 18.8%** to reach **1,200**.
- **Raise average spend per order to £69.00**.
- **Decrease dependency on top 5 SKUs** to no more than **55%** of revenue.
- **Expand winter accessories and layering pieces** to achieve at least **10% of Q4 revenue**.
- **Ensure at least 30% of total annual revenue** comes from new products introduced in 2024.

The overarching theme for the year is **"Threaded for All Seasons,"** focusing on diversifying the product range and enhancing brand relevance. The plan also addresses risk considerations related to performance and inventory management.

#### 2. Goals and Targets Met and Surpassed in the Current Period (Q3 2024):
- **Revenue Target**: The total revenue for Q3 2024 was **£22,791**, which is on track towards the annual goal of **£78,000**.
- **Average Spend per Order**: The average spend per order was **£64.78**, which is close to the target of **£69.00**.

#### 3. Goals and Targets Unmet in the Current Period (Q3 2024):
- **Total Orders**: The total number of orders for Q3 was **354**, which may not meet the target of **1,200** for the year.
- **Dependency on Top SKUs**: There is no specific data on the dependency on top 5 SKUs, but it is critical to monitor this as it affects revenue diversification.

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.
